feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: it shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/communications leadership. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited outcome-focused evidence beyond selected metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Strong relevance to target roles: Drupal, analytics, editorial systems, AI-enabled search, and public-sector communications are consistently reinforced.  
- Credibility is boosted by concrete scale indicators such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers.”

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Header, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; consolidate to sharpen focus and save space.  
- Add more measurable outcomes in each role: e.g., traffic growth, engagement uplift, production efficiency, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” vs. other compound modifiers, and list punctuation (some bullets use serial commas, some do not). No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler and can be removed.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets. Tightening it around scale and public-sector impact would make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “Senior digital leader” with a more specific positioning tied to public-sector digital platforms and communications systems.
- Add one concrete scale signal from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page website,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Simplify the long capability list; group related areas to improve flow and reduce buzzword density.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector web ecosystems, governance, and content operations. Leads enterprise website transformation, analytics and reporting infrastructure, editorial workflows, and multimedia programs for high-volume, mission-driven organizations, including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Senior digital leader” repeats the subtitle’s leadership positioning.
- The capability list closely duplicates Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize higher-level leadership capabilities rather than repeating detailed skill categories.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Reframe as broader, executive-level competencies: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and content operations • Analytics, measurement and reporting • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and discovery • Workflow automation and systems integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style: use “and” instead of mixing “&” with “and” for a cleaner, more consistent tone.
- Consider replacing “editorial systems” with “content operations” to better align with the experience section’s governance/workflow emphasis.
- If space is tight, shorten “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to “AI-enabled search and discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially duplicates the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid tool-specific or channel-specific detail.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is also covered in Topline Skills and work experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinct and higher impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed X using Y to achieve Z.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “designed for continued campaign growth” with more concrete value, e.g., “built on a reusable modular framework for future campaign expansion.”
- Standardize style: spell out “10 x 20-foot,” and consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current freelance role and NACo bullets.
- Anniversary campaign may be the most distinct item; consider emphasizing projects not already named in Work Experience.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a services list rather than a results-driven position. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact themes and align it with the named projects already highlighted elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client type: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into sharper outcomes, e.g.:
- “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including scalable microsite templates, modular content components and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Improved enterprise web operations by redesigning workflows, analytics and governance for coordinated cross-channel communications.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery experience.”
- Replace generic phrases like “support,” “advise,” and “deliver” with stronger verbs: led, built, redesigned, launched, improved.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages/templates, publishing time reduced, traffic/users served, search accuracy gains, stakeholder teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating NACo-era governance/analytics language too closely; emphasize consulting ownership and current AI/search work.
- “Microsites” and campaign storytelling already appear in Recent Projects, so keep this entry higher-level.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be even stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad opener with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization as the anchor achievement; compress metrics into one line: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add % improvements, cost savings, production volume, turnaround time, engagement growth, or reporting adoption for analytics/studio/governance bullets.
- Tighten channel language: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials” rather than listing platforms generically.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo bullets; emphasize building the in-house studio, not recurring video production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more role-specific by emphasizing operational leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth before the larger strategic/platform remit.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and measurable if possible: “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add views, cadence, or audience growth if available.
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper operations point: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” echo the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership strengths rather than repeating broad digital/communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector stakeholder and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Use parallel noun phrases; avoid mixing “messaging,” “planning,” and “leadership” styles.
- Consider swapping in one more distinctive capability tied to recent work, such as “content operations” or “enterprise web governance.”
- If space allows elsewhere, support this section with outcomes from recent roles rather than broad descriptors.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT” and Core Competencies. Make it more selective and outcome-oriented, emphasizing the platforms and execution areas most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to grouped, higher-signal capabilities: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and keep only platforms/tools tied to recent work; consider dropping SharePoint or Power Pages if they are not evidenced in recent experience.
- Replace “AI-enabled search experiences” with “AI-enabled search and discovery” for stronger business relevance.
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “CMS modernization and migration” aligns better with the 10,000+ page Drupal migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool lists for the Technical section.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search” already appear in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it largely repeats both Core Competencies and the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” technical list. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value capabilities over tool names alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance analysis
- Put the most senior/value-added items first: “Analytics strategy,” “KPI design,” and “executive reporting” should lead, with tools grouped after.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Board/executive reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If accurate, consider adding one outcome-oriented qualifier such as “decision-ready dashboards” or “analytics infrastructure” to align with recent Director-level work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure.”
- It also duplicates the “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization” section; keep Topline Skills more strategic and Technical + IT more tool-specific.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership and delivery scope, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to sound more senior.
- Replace “Hybrid and virtual event production” with “Livestream and hybrid event production” for cleaner phrasing and less duplication.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this skill area to outcomes from recent roles (e.g., built NACo’s first in-house studio; expanded advocacy/event production capacity).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are supported by recent NACo bullets, so this section should stay concise, not restate experience.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This section should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repeating the same skills elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/recent platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add level/context instead of just names: “Drupal (primary) • WordPress (working) • SharePoint/Power Pages (working) • GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it feels lighter than the rest and may dilute enterprise positioning.
- Keep ordering by relevance/recency, with Drupal clearly first given the 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms.
- If both sections stay, use this one for platform names only and let the Topline Skills section carry broader modernization/CMS language.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, not repeat broad web basics.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied delivery, e.g. “Front-End & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Integrations.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context instead of only tools, e.g. “API integrations for CMS/workflow automation” or “GitHub Actions for deployment automation.”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they date the entry without adding value.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates Topline Skills item [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations”). Keep one broad summary there and make this section more tool-specific.
- “Cloudflare Workers” and “GitHub Actions” are strong differentiators—keep them prominent, as they add more value than basic HTML/CSS.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” already stated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Make it more selective and grouped around recent, relevant systems.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by function and trim older/generic items: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams
- Consider dropping Basecamp and Trello unless they were materially used in recent roles; they dilute the enterprise/public-sector positioning.
- If space allows, add light context instead of a pure list: “Workflow automation and team operations: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Microsoft Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira, Asana, Basecamp, Trello are all project-management tools; listing all four can feel redundant.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale of your email leadership. It should signal enterprise email/engagement capability, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • enterprise newsletter and member communications systems**
- If accurate, add one qualifier for level/scope: **used to support newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders**
- Keep platform names only if you’ve used each directly; otherwise remove weaker/older tools to prioritize the most recent enterprise system

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here if that metric already appears prominently in Work Experience
- “Engagement” may overlap with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communications operations”; keep this item tool-focused, not strategic

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show level of capability. Tighten it into a cleaner technical stack and use more specific terms.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • SEO analysis • Experimentation (A/B testing) • KPI/dashboard reporting
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI/dashboard reporting” to sound more strategic and less generic.
- If accurate, consider swapping one generic term for a stronger capability: “Conversion analysis,” “Performance reporting,” or “Tagging/measurement strategy.”
- Keep only platforms and analytical methods here; save outcomes like improved decision-making for recent NACo and consulting bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider removing one section or making this one tools-only and the other capability-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already substantiated in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating extra descriptors here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to foundational team-building, site refresh support, and early multimedia production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution, not generic support: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, livestream/event volume, weekly video cadence, audience reach, or team size supported.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”
- If true, add a measurable operational outcome such as faster publishing, more consistent output, expanded in-house production, or reduced vendor reliance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the later “weekly advocacy video update”; differentiate this as the launch/build phase.
- “strengthening workflows” and team guidance overlap with 2018–2024 entries; keep this item focused on early infrastructure and hands-on production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer action such as “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or programs supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on research/program support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating team leadership here, since stronger management responsibility appears in later NACo positions.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia & Creative Software
- Rewrite as: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
- If you want to retain capabilities, split them into a separate skills line elsewhere: Livestream production • Studio operations • Podcast production
- Only keep tools you actively used in recent roles; add others only if they strengthen current-market relevance

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” overlaps with Topline Skills (“Livestreaming,” “Studio operations,” “Hybrid and virtual event production”).
- “Podcast production” is already evidenced in older experience; keep it only if still part of your current offer or recent work.
